channel.title: Global Arbitration Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Arbitration Review (globalarbitrationreview.com)

item.title: White & Case and 3VB in place for Bangladeshi disputes
item.description: Bangladesh has turned to White & Case to defend it against an investment treaty claim by one of the country’s richest men, while a state agency has appointed a team from London barristers' set Three Verulam Buildings for a SIAC dispute with an Indian power company.

item.title: European insurers withdraw ICSID claims against Mexico
item.description: European insurance giants Allianz and AXA have discontinued ICSID claims that they filed against Mexico in response to retrospective tax demands.

item.title: ICC panel rejects Ecuadorean cable car claim
item.description: The Ecuadorean municipality of Guayaquil has defeated a US$40 million ICC claim filed by a French-Panamanian consortium over a cable car system.

item.title: Arnold & Porter promotes from Lone Star team
item.description: Arnold & Porter has promoted Katelyn Horne to partner in Washington, DC, and John Muse-Fisher to counsel in San Francisco – both part of the team that successfully advised South Korea in the high-profile Lone Star case.

item.title: Lugovoy Law survives third constitutional challenge
item.description: Russia’s Constitutional Court has rejected a third complaint over the Lugovoy Law, the mechanism that allows the country’s courts to assert exclusive jurisdiction over commercial disputes involving sanctioned Russian parties.

item.title: Burundi faces another mining claim
item.description: A second investor has filed a contractual ICSID claim against Burundi after the east African state sought to renegotiate its partnerships with several mining companies.

item.title: London set suspends French arbitrator over Epstein emails
item.description: Prominent French arbitrator Matthieu de Boisséson says he will challenge a decision by London set Littleton Chambers to suspend him following the publication of emails suggesting he was in contact with convicted child sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

item.title: Álvarez returns to ICSID as deputy secretary-general
item.description: Gabriela Álvarez Ávila has been elected as deputy secretary-general to ICSID, to which she returns 25 years after she first joined and after nearly a decade in private practice at DLA Piper and Curtis.

item.title: Clyde & Co practice chair departs for Keystone
item.description: Ben Knowles, chair of the global arbitration group at Clyde & Co, has left the firm after more than three decades to join Keystone Law in London.

item.title: Dutch retailer takes Serbia to ICSID
item.description: A Dutch retailer says it has launched an ICSID claim against Serbia over a government decree capping profit margins on food and consumer goods.
